title: About Me
text:
I’m a PhD student in the field of Clinical Immunology at Karolinska Institutet, Sweden. I’m interested in base editing approaches and off-target validation methods for X-Linked agammaglobulinemia (XLA). I’m also interested in bioinformatics and computational biology.
This blog is part of the course “Reproducible Research” organized by the Swedish National Graduate School in Medical Bioinformatics (MedBioInfo). The blog is designed to provide a platform to the class of 2026 to share what we have learned during the course and showcase our work.

title: Software Environments and Containers
text:
1. Installation
wget -qO- https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh
2. Source the pixi environment to your shell configuration file. For Linux:
~/.bashrc
For MacOS:
~/.zshrc
3. Initialize a pixi environment and add conda and bioconda channels to the project.
pixi init <name of the project> -c conda-forge -c bioconda 
Inside the newly created directory there is now one pixi.toml file, that we can inspect using bash cat pixi.toml. Inside the pixi.toml we can find information about the project.
4.Add dependencies
pixi add <dependency>
Run bash pixi run <dependency> --version to check if the dependency was installed correctly.
Alternatively, use pixi shell to enter the pixi environment and run the command <dependency> --version to check if the dependency was installed correctly.

title: Git Basics and How to build a Quarto Blog
section: Publish your Quarto Blog to GitHub Pages
text:
Publish your Quarto Blog to GitHub Pages
1. Create a repository on GitHub. No need to initialize the repository with a README, .gitignore, or license.
2. In VS Code, open the blog’s project folder. In the terminal, run these commands, replacing USERNAME with your GitHub username:
git init -b main
git add .
git commit -m "Add Quarto blog"
git remote add origin https://github.com/USERNAME/RR_Blog_2026.git
git push -u origin main
3. Create .github/workflows/publish.yml in the project and add the workflow shown below.
name: Publish Quarto site

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Quarto
        uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2

      - name: Publish to GitHub Pages
        uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/publish@v2
        with:
          target: gh-pages
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
4. Push the workflow to GitHub:
git add .github/workflows/publish.yml
git commit -m "Add GitHub Pages publishing workflow"
git push
5. On GitHub, go to Settings → Pages. Under Build and deployment, choose Deploy from a branch, then select the gh-pages branch and /(root) folder.
7. Go to Actions to check the status of your workflow. If it fails, check the logs for errors and fix them.
7. When the GitHub Actions workflow succeeds, you can access your blog from Pages → Visit site

title: Software Environments and Containers
text:
Educational metaphor
I like to imagine a pixi environmnent as Hermione’s magic bag from Harry Potter. From the outside, our project directory looks small.
pixi_nextflow/ ├── pixi.toml └── pixi.lock/
But, inside the Pixi environment we can have things such as:

Python
Nextflow
Java
R
bioinformatics tools
dependencies

By using channels using the -c flag when initializing the pixi environment, we can install dependencies from different sources. We specify which magical shops to visit when we need to put something into the bag.

text:
Nextflow is a workflow management system that enables scalable and reproducible scientific workflows. It allows us to write complex pipelines in a simple and readable manner, while also providing support for parallel execution and integration with various computing environments.

title: Feedback and Credits
text:
The process of building a Quarto blog and publishing it to GitHub Pages has been one of the most creative things I have done in a while.
My perfectionism and desire to create a visually appealing blog that at the same time reveals my personality has led me to spend a lot of time on the design and layout. I have been experimenting with different themes, layouts, and colors before settling on this final design.
After enough thinking, I decided to use matrix raining code on the backround of the welcome page and use the neon green and black aesthetics in my blog, as a tribute to one of my favorite childhood movies “The Matrix”.
I wanted to desing interesting thumbnails for my posts, so I tried to match every post with a painting that I thought would fit the topic. I chose The Japanese footbridge by Monet for the GitHub Basics and How to build a Quarto Blog post as a metaphor for these reproducible research tools that help us connect the different parts of our research and make them more accessible to others. The The Dream by Henri Rousseau in the Software Environments and Containers shows woman reclining on a couch in Paris, dreaming she is listening to a flute player in the jungle. I used this painting as a metaphor for the software environments and containers that allow us to run our code in different environments, just like the woman in the painting is dreaming of being in a different place. There are two art pieces of Gustav Klimt as well. The Park used in Nextflow and nf-core pipelines reminds me of the representation of the channels in the Nextflow pipelines and the Medicine painting used in Feedback and Credits is one of my favorite paintings of all time. Just notice the Hygeia female figure down in the middle of the painting, who is the goddess of health. Circles in a circle by Wassily Kandinsky used in Plotting with ggplot2 reminds me a lot of the plots we can create with ggplot2.
We have talked about cinema and art. We should also talk about music. Currently, I am listening to the Irish band Fontaines D.C. One of my favourite discoveries lately. Fontaines D.C draw heavy inspiration from working-class Irish literature and traditional music, to sing about Dead-End Loves and Fantasies, Mental Health and engage in Political Criticism.
